name: Raven Row
funding: Funded by Alex Sainsbury, who says the money is his, through the Glass-House Trust he settled.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the About page names its one funder, and four board members are named.

name: Red Brick Art Museum
funding: Private museum built by collectors Yan Shijie and Cao Mei, who invested nearly RMB 400 million over eight years.
watch: The 20,000 sq m site was designed by Dong Yugan of Peking University. Yan is described only as a collector and entrepreneur.
records_note: The museum site has visitor, exhibition and research pages only; no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board are published.

name: Rijksakademie van beeldende kunsten
funding: About EUR 5.2M income in 2024, mostly Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science money, with Ammodo as main partner, plus Rabobank and De Nederlandsche Bank.
watch: Multi-year studio residency for ~50 artists from around the world, with public open studios and lectures. Main partner Ammodo (2022-26). Brouwerij 't IJ (alcohol) backs Open Studios. A Dec 2024 alumni campaign challenged its governance.
records_note: The Rijksakademie posts annual reports for 2015 to 2025, an ANBI form, a named supporter list and its four-member supervisory board.

name: Rwanda Art Museum
funding: Owned and run by the Rwanda Cultural Heritage Academy, the government body that runs Rwanda's national museums.
watch: Opened in 2009 in the former presidential palace at Kanombe and renamed the Rwanda Art Museum in 2018.
records_note: Publishes nothing itself: its parent, the Rwanda Cultural Heritage Academy, posts laws and policies but no annual reports, accounts, funders or board.

name: Schaulager
funding: Made possible by the Laurenz Foundation, founded in 1999 by Maja Oeri and Hans U. Bodenmann. The foundation does not give grants; no other funders are named.
watch: Herzog & de Meuron built it in 2002-03. The Emanuel Hoffmann Foundation collection is its core.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts or donors; its Laurenz Foundation pages name the foundation board and say the foundation makes Schaulager possible.

name: SculptureCenter
funding: Expenses $2.6M (FY2025). Teiger, Kellen, Warhol, Lambent, Hartwig, Woodner and Frankenthaler funds; NYSCA and NYC Cultural Affairs; an international council of collectors.
watch: Arison Arts Foundation and David Rockefeller Fund give through a New York arts network. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: No annual reports found; 990s are on ProPublica, the support page names donors without a date, and the board is listed.

name: Secession (Wiener Secession)
funding: City of Vienna and the federal ministry. Erste Bank is main sponsor; annual partners Neuroth, Dorotheum and LG; 2026 partners Arbeiterkammer and UNIQA.
watch: The world's oldest independent artist-run exhibition house, founded in 1897 by Gustav Klimt and fellow Secessionists. Its motto: 'To every age its art, to art its freedom'.
records_note: Shows partners mostly as logos under 2026 headings and states a third of its budget is public; no reports, accounts or board named.

name: Selasar Sunaryo Art Space
funding: Founded 1998 by artist Sunaryo with direction and support from the Selasar Sunaryo Foundation.
watch: Nonprofit art space in Bandung. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found. Earlier partner names (Goethe-Institut, Japan Foundation, British Council) are not on its site.
records_note: Its site posts no annual report, accounts, sponsor list or board; a 2010 ASEF profile names only the Selasar Sunaryo Foundation.

name: Sesc São Paulo
funding: 2023 revenue R$3.44bn: R$2.70bn (78%) from the compulsory levy on commerce, services and tourism firms, R$209M from services, R$495M financial income.
records_note: Posts annual management reports for 2020 to 2024 with an independent audit report; funded by a business levy and names no sponsors.

name: Siida Sámi Museum (Saamelaismuseo Siida)
funding: A small state-backed museum: most of its money comes from Finland's Ministry of Education and Culture, plus a yearly grant from Inari Municipality.
watch: Owned by the Sámi Museum Foundation, whose board must be at least half Sámi. Its exhibition renewal was paid for by Finnish foundations.
records_note: Siida's site posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board names; it says only that the foundation board has eight members.

name: Sir John Soane's Museum
funding: £4.2M income (2024-25). DCMS grant-in-aid £1.165M; trusts and patrons including Linbury, Leverhulme, Wates, Deborah Loeb Brice Foundation; brand licensing partners.
watch: Non-departmental public body set up by an 1833 Act of Parliament. Submits audited accounts to Parliament each year.
records_note: Annual reports with accounts from 2011-12 to 2024-25 on its site, donors named in the 2024-25 report, and trustees listed.

name: Sofia City Art Gallery
funding: Sofia Municipality funds yearly acquisitions, resumed in 2007. Partners listed: Ministry of Culture, America for Bulgaria Foundation, Aurubis Bulgaria, Institut français and Goethe-Institut. No budget is published.
watch: Founded 1928 as part of Sofia's city museum. Holds more than 23,000 works by Bulgarian artists.
records_note: Its Partners page shows six unlabelled partner logos and media logos; no annual reports, accounts or board are posted, only a staff list.
